chosen.premise: Graveler climbs a mountain while eating rocks, then rolls all the way back to the bottom.
chosen.hook: Graveler’s daily routine is one enormous mountain round trip.
chosen.visualIdea: Animate Graveler crunching rocks uphill, reaching the summit, then curling into a ball and rolling down.
chosen.note: A highly Graveler-specific routine with two directly matching Pokédex entries; the uphill eating and downhill roll create a clear visual story.

candidates.premise: Graveler climbs a mountain while eating rocks, then rolls all the way back to the bottom.
candidates.hook: Graveler’s daily routine is one enormous mountain round trip.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate Graveler crunching rocks uphill, reaching the summit, then curling into a ball and rolling down.
candidates.note: A highly Graveler-specific routine with two directly matching Pokédex entries; the uphill eating and downhill roll create a clear visual story.

candidates.premise: Graveler repeatedly climbs toward a mountain peak only to roll back down the same mountain.
candidates.hook: Graveler reaches the top of the mountain just to undo the entire climb.
candidates.visualIdea: Track Graveler’s uphill route on a mountain diagram, then reverse the path in one long downhill roll.
candidates.note: A concrete, amusing contradiction in Graveler's routine, but it is narrower and less layered than the mountain round trip because it omits the rock-eating behavior.

candidates.premise: Graveler’s rolling journey has a bizarre fail state: falling into a river makes it explode.
candidates.hook: There is one place Graveler absolutely should not roll into.
candidates.visualIdea: Contrast Graveler surviving cliffs and boulders with a river warning sign, followed by a sudden explosion effect.
candidates.note: The river explosion is the biggest shock, but it relies on a single unusual entry and offers less narrative substance for a full episode.

candidates.premise: Graveler treats losing body parts during mountain rolls as completely normal.
candidates.hook: Graveler can lose pieces of itself and simply keep rolling.
candidates.visualIdea: As Graveler tumbles downhill, small rocky pieces chip off while it continues without reacting.
candidates.note: Genuinely disturbing and well supported, though 'body parts' is somewhat stronger wording than the entries' 'pieces' and 'chipping off.'

candidates.premise: Graveler eats a ton of rocks every day, especially rocks covered in moss.
candidates.hook: Graveler does not live on rocks—it eats a ton of them daily.
candidates.visualIdea: Pile up mossy boulders like a meal, then show Graveler crunching through them with a daily counter.
candidates.note: The daily rock diet and moss preference are directly supported and easy to depict, but eating rocks is an expected trait for a Rock Pokémon and less distinctive than the round trip.

candidates.premise: Once Graveler builds momentum, it rolls straight through obstacles and can exceed 60 miles per hour.
candidates.hook: At full speed, Graveler does not dodge obstacles—it deletes them.
candidates.visualIdea: Show a speed gauge passing 60 mph as trees, boulders, and trail obstacles vanish from Graveler’s path.
candidates.note: Strong action premise and excellent visuals, but the hook exaggerates the evidence slightly, and the basic unstoppable-roller idea overlaps with Graveler's broader identity.
